summary: Backend-only regression for Plaid banking integration + Customer Support Phase 1. Wrote 26 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration22_plaid_support.py covering /api/plaid/{status,link-token,exchange-public-token,accounts,sync,item/{id}}, /api/accounts/all, and the full /api/support/{tickets,tickets/{id},tickets/{id}/reply,admin/*} lifecycle including attachment validation and admin private-note isolation. 26/26 passed against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Verified Mongo persistence: bank_transactions had 48 rows with provider='plaid' after sandbox sync, support_counters auto-incremented (seq=6), admin user support@jaleter.com has is_admin=true. Access tokens are never returned to callers — only access_token_encrypted is stored server-side. Expo web preview responds 200 at localhost:3000 (verified boot).
critical_code_review_comments: plaid_service.encrypt raises PlaidError('Server encryption key missing') if SIMPLEFIN_ENC_KEY/PLAID_ENC_KEY is unset. Currently set in .env so working — /api/plaid/exchange-public-token catches this as HTTP 500 which is correct.
support_service._validate_attachment rejects oversize before base64 decoding via a pre-check on payload length (4/3 * MAX_BYTES + 32); 5MB oversized payload correctly returns 413.
admin_add_reply moves ticket to 'waiting_on_user' only when status is not resolved/closed — verified.
get_ticket_for_user correctly strips replies with is_private=True before serializing — verified end-to-end (admin's PRIVATE_NOTE_… string not visible to user, but visible to admin).
/api/plaid/accounts and /api/plaid/exchange-public-token response payloads do NOT include access_token or access_token_encrypted — confirmed via test assertions.

success_rate.frontend: n/a (not tested this run; Expo web boots 200)

Admin user support@jaleter.com is auto-seeded on backend startup.
